edges.rationale: Multiplexing/demultiplexing explains how the transport layer implements the logical end-to-end process-to-process communication introduced in the overview; students must first know what the transport layer does and how it relates to the network layer before studying how segments are delivered to sockets.

UDP's minimal service model only makes sense against the backdrop of the transport/network layer relationship and the overview of Internet transport protocols (UDP vs. TCP) presented in the introduction.
Understanding UDP requires knowing how UDP segments are delivered to the correct socket via connectionless two-tuple demultiplexing, which is covered in the multiplexing/demultiplexing topic.

TCP's connection-oriented demultiplexing based on four-tuples (source IP, source port, dest IP, dest port) is a prerequisite concept from the multiplexing/demultiplexing topic needed to understand how TCP segments reach the right connection.

TCP's reliable data transfer mechanism is a direct application of the RDT principles: acknowledgments, retransmissions, sequence numbers, pipelining, and the GBN/SR sliding-window ideas underpin TCP's error recovery, timeout management, and flow control.

TCP's congestion control (slow start, AIMD congestion avoidance, fast recovery) manipulates a congestion window alongside TCP's reliable data transfer, RTT estimation, and receive-window flow control; TCP's operation must be understood first for the congestion control mechanisms to make sense.
